title: The key dimensions of human action: Content and form
title_zh: 人类行为的关键维度：内容与形式
abstract: Human action, both in execution and observation, is characterized by two fundamental attributes: the action goal (the "what") and its vitality form (VF), namely the "how" an action is performed. Over the past three decades, substantial progress has been made in elucidating the neural bases of action goals. Converging evidence identifies a parieto-frontal network, possibly extending to additional brain regions, which encodes the goal-related content of both observed and executed actions (the mirror circuit). In contrast, considerably less attention has been devoted to the neural mechanisms underlying vitality forms. Nevertheless, growing evidence indicates that VFs are processed by a distinct insulo-cingulate network. Together, the parieto-frontal and insulo-cingulate circuits constitute a functional architecture that integrates goal representation with affective-motor expression. This integration enables social understanding and supports adaptive interpersonal behavior. The present review is organized into three sections. First, we examine the neural circuits underlying action goals and vitality forms. Second, we review evidence that interactions between these two neural systems underwrite action and its observation. Third, we discuss the role of vitality forms in the development of humanoid robots.
abstract_zh: 人类行为，无论是执行还是观察，都具有两个基本属性：行为目标（"what"）和其活力形式（VF，即"how"）。过去三十年，关于行为目标神经基础的研究取得了显著进展。多条证据表明，顶叶-前额网络（可能延伸至其他脑区）编码观察和执行行为的目标相关内容（镜像回路）。相比之下，关于活力形式的神经机制研究相对较少。然而，越来越多的证据表明，VF由一个独立的岛叶-扣带网络处理。顶叶-前额回路与岛叶-扣带回路共同构成一种功能架构，将目标表征与情感-运动表达整合。该整合实现社会理解并支持适应性人际行为。本文综述分为三部分：首先，探讨行为目标和活力形式的神经回路；其次，回顾这两种神经系统相互作用如何支撑行为及其观察；第三，讨论活力形式在类人机器人发展中的作用。
